result:
I fixed it: when the language save is refused, the page now keeps the language the user chose, and the "not saved" notice appears in that language. Every required check passed in both locale settings, after one lint failure that I fixed and re-ran. Nothing is committed; the handback is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG2/T-DG2-FE11-frontend-ux-engineer.md`.

**Decision: option (a).** The page does not revert, and the notice is in the chosen language.
- A user who switches EN→AR may only read Arabic. Under (b) the page would snap back to English with an English notice they can't read.
- The saved preference still wins on sign-in, on reload and when it actually changes. The notice now says so: "…Your saved language returns the next time you open the app."

**Root cause.** `RequireSession` re-applied the saved preference in an effect keyed on `[preferred, i18n]`. react-i18next 17 returns a new `i18n` object on every language change, so every switch triggered that effect and put the old language back straight away. The same bug also briefly flipped a *successful* switch back (ar → en → ar) while the save was in flight.

**Fix (only `apps/web/**`):**
- `session.tsx` applies the preference only when it is first known or its value changes.
- `LanguageSwitch.tsx` builds the notice from its translation key when it renders, so it can't get stuck in the old language. `dir` and `lang` follow the language on screen.
- While signed in, the notice sits in a polite live region that stays in the page, so it is announced once.
  - I didn't give it `role="status"`: an always-present status element would clash with the sign-in and Team pages, which look up their own status message that way.
  - A small CSS rule stops the empty region taking space in the header.
- Both `common.json` files have the reworded `notSaved` text and one new key, `notSavedReverted`. That covers the rare case where another tab changes the saved preference while the notice is showing.

**Sweep.** No other notice is shown in the wrong language after a failed preference or profile save.
- The only call to `PUT /me/preferences` is the language switch.
- The admin Users create/edit errors are translated when they render, so they follow the page language.
- Three unrelated messages store already-translated text, so they stay in the old language if the user switches while they're visible: TeamPage's "Role assigned", LoginPage's invalid-username error and the JourneysSection error. I left them alone and suggest a Low polish item.

**Tests:**
- **Component tests:** 8 new, all under StrictMode. They cover EN→AR and AR→EN refused with 403 csrf, 403 forbidden and 503; switching back; the successful-switch flicker; the reverted case; and the sign-in page having no live region.
- **e2e:** FE10's test 4 now asserts the exact notice text in the chosen language, `lang`/`dir`, a single live region, axe, a screenshot, and that nothing has flipped back a second later.
- **Negative controls:** run against HEAD's sources, 7 of the 8 component tests fail and test 4 fails in both projects. With only HEAD's `session.tsx` swapped in, the failures show the actual revert and the wrong-language notice on the real stack. With all of HEAD's files, most failures are just the missing notice element, so the `session.tsx`-only run is the real behavioural proof.

**Checks (both locale settings):**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck, build, format:check | exit 0 |
| lint | exit 0 on the re-run (see below) |
| `pnpm test` on Node 22 and 24 | 816/816 passed |
| contrast | PASS |
| e2e P1 + P2 + `p2-blank-text` + `session-end`, chromium-en and chromium-ar | 68 passed |
| axe (16 summaries) | 0 violations of any impact |
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG1` | PASS, exit 0 |

**Non-zero exits and warnings:**
- The first lint run failed with exit 1 on an unused `escape` import I left in the e2e spec. I removed it and re-ran every check; the results above are from the re-run.
- These warnings were already there before this change:
  - a Fastify `FSTDEP022` deprecation warning from an API test;
  - Vite's "chunks larger than 500 kB";
  - three `npm warn Unknown project config` lines from `npx`.
- There are no React warnings or hook timeouts in any log.

**Known gaps:**
- At 1280 px the longer notice wraps to two lines and squeezes the wordmark, visible in both screenshots. It is readable and axe is clean, but a designer may want it shorter or moved to a banner.
- After a reload, the browser's stored hint can briefly show the chosen language before the saved one is applied. That behaviour is the same as on HEAD.

Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG2/T-DG2-FE11-evidence/`:
- en-to-ar-language-not-saved.png
- ar-to-en-language-not-saved.png
- the check logs, negative-control logs and axe summaries
